kaps_punt: Plaaslike omgewingsgesondheidsprobleme: Plaaslike gesondheidsprobleme wat gereeld voorkom soos tuberkulose, diarree, malaria, masels, ensovoorts; Oorsake van gesondheidsprobleme; Simptome van gesondheidsprobleme; en Beskikbare behandeling vir gesondheidsprobleme.

items.bewering: Twee siektes wat deur die lug loop (titel)
items.blok: titel
items.bron: TB: NSW Health TB Fact Sheet (Mar 2024) 'TB is spread through the air when a person with TB disease of the lungs or throat coughs, sneezes, sings or speaks'. Measles: CDC measles causes/transmission page (spreads through coughing and sneezing, virus lives up to two hours in an airspace); NHS measles page (spreads when an infected person breathes, coughs or sneezes).

items.bewering: Tuberkulose en masels loop albei deur die lug van een mens na 'n ander.
items.blok: Van mens tot mens deur die lug
items.bron: NSW Health TB Fact Sheet 2024; CDC TB 101 for health care workers (TB spread through the air from person to person); CDC measles transmission page. CDC adds measles can also spread via contaminated surfaces; the sentence does not say 'only', so it is not made false by that.

items.bewering: Hierna skryf ons tuberkulose as TB.
items.blok: Van mens tot mens deur die lug
items.bron: TB is the standard abbreviation for tuberculosis (NSW Health 'Tuberculosis (TB) Fact Sheet'; Western Cape Government health article on tuberculosis).

items.bewering: Wanneer iemand wat siek is hoes of nies, spat klein druppeltjies uit sy mond. Praat en sing maak dieselfde druppeltjies.
items.blok: Van mens tot mens deur die lug
items.bron: CDC TB 101: tiny particles containing TB bacteria are expelled when someone with infectious TB coughs, sneezes, speaks or sings; NSW Health 2024 same list; Western Cape Government tuberculosis article 'coughs, sneezes, or talks'. Note for the human only: the TB particles are droplet nuclei small enough to stay in the air for hours (CDC), which 'klein druppeltjies' covers adequately at this level.

items.bewering: Iemand naby hom asem hulle in en kry so die siekte.
items.blok: Van mens tot mens deur die lug
items.bron: CDC TB 101 ('people nearby may breathe in these TB bacteria and become infected'); NSW Health 2024 ('when other people breathe in these germs they can become infected'); CDC measles: up to 90% of non-immune close contacts become infected. Tested specifically for certainty-vs-possibility: read as a description of the route ('so' = this is how), it is true. Read alone it could suggest every nearby person who inhales falls ill, which is false for TB (about 10% of infected people develop disease, NSW Health). The lesson qualifies it explicitly in the next block ('Nie almal wat die kieme inasem, word siek nie') and for measles in the vaccine block ('kry gewoonlik nie masels nie'), so the lesson as a whole does not teach the certainty. Those two qualifiers carry this sentence and must not be cut. 'Naby' is accurate for TB (most people catch it from someone they spend a lot of time with, NSW Health) and is not stated as a limit.

items.bewering: In 'n klein kamer sonder vars lug gebeur dit makliker en 'n oop venster maak 'n verskil.
items.blok: Van mens tot mens deur die lug
items.bron: Western Cape Government tuberculosis article (prevention advice: keep rooms well-ventilated, spend time outdoors); CDC MMWR infection-control guideline (droplet nuclei kept airborne by indoor air currents for long periods); Mangaung PHC study (PMC5633895) on crowding facilitating transmission.

items.bewering: TB kom van kieme wat in 'n mens se longe kan groei.
items.blok: Waar TB vandaan kom
items.bron: NSW Health 2024: TB is caused by the bacteria Mycobacterium tuberculosis and most commonly affects the lungs, but can also affect other parts of the body. 'Kan groei' is not an exclusive claim.

items.bewering: Baie mense glo jy kry TB uit 'n beker, 'n bord of kos wat julle deel.
items.blok: Waar TB vandaan kom
items.bron: DHS analysis Lesotho, Malawi, Namibia, Zambia 2013-2016 (PMC6208015): 17.8% of adults believed TB spreads through sharing utensils. South Africa: Mangaung PHC study (PMC5633895) cites earlier South African research in which patients described TB spreading through shared meals and drinking vessels, and itself found 85% believed TB spreads by sharing toothbrushes. No South African percentage for cups and plates was found; 'baie mense' is a soft quantifier and roughly one adult in six in neighbouring countries supports it.

items.bewering: Dit is nie waar nie, want die TB-kieme kom deur die lug.
items.blok: Waar TB vandaan kom
items.bron: NSW Health 2024: 'TB is not spread by household items (for example by cutlery, crockery, drinking glasses...)'; CDC guidance as reproduced by state health departments: not spread by sharing food or drink. Caveat for the human, not a finding: a separate, much rarer form, zoonotic TB (Mycobacterium bovis), does reach people through unpasteurised milk, and South African research documents this risk in rural cattle-keeping households (University of Pretoria, Pathogens 2019; KwaZulu-Natal study of M. bovis survival in souring milk, PMC4488074). The sentence is about catching TB from a person through shared things, and that is true; it does not mention raw milk.

items.bewering: Nie almal wat die kieme inasem, word siek nie.
items.blok: Waar TB vandaan kom
items.bron: NSW Health 2024: in most people with TB infection the body's defences control the germs; only about 10 per cent of people with TB infection will get TB disease; people with TB infection are not infectious.

items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Signs and symptoms' and EBSCO Research Starters 'Understanding disease signs and symptoms': a symptom is subjective, experienced and reported by the patient (e.g. fatigue, pain, nausea).

items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: Wikipedia 'Signs and symptoms'; EBSCO Research Starters; RxList definition of sign: a sign is objective and can be observed or measured by someone other than the patient.

items.bewering: Koors en 'n uitslag is tekens.
items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: EBSCO Research Starters lists fever and rash as outward signs; a measured raised temperature is a sign (feeling feverish is the symptom). The lesson ties fever to feeling or measuring it from outside, which keeps it a sign.

items.bewering: Die belangrikste waarskuwing van TB is 'n hoes wat nie weggaan nie.
items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: Western Cape Government TB Control Programme page: a cough lasting longer than two weeks is described as the main sign; Western Cape tuberculosis article lists 'Cough that won't go away' first; NSW Health 2024 lists a persistent cough first. 'Belangrikste waarskuwing' matches 'main sign'.

items.bewering: Nie elke hoes is TB nie.
items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: PMC4985807 review of acute cough: the vast majority of acute cough is due to viral upper respiratory tract infection (the common cold).

items.bewering: Die meeste hoes kom van 'n verkoue en gaan vanself weg.
items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: PMC4985807 (acute cough review): 'in the vast majority of cases, acute cough is due to acute viral upper respiratory tract infection, i.e. the common cold'; NICE NG120 draft: acute cough is usually self-limiting. Note for the human: a cold cough can last 3 to 4 weeks (NICE), so the following sentence's two-week clinic rule is screening advice, not a claim that cold coughs end within two weeks; the lesson does not make that claim.

items.bewering: 'n Hoes wat twee weke of langer aanhou, moet kliniek toe gaan.
items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: Western Cape Department of Health and Wellness tuberculosis article: if you have had any of these symptoms (including a cough that won't go away) for more than 2 weeks, go to your clinic; Western Cape TB Control Programme page: cough lasting longer than two weeks. South African guidance uses two weeks (NSW Australia uses three; one older Western Cape awareness page also said three, but the current provincial pages say two).

items.bewering: Gaan vroeër as jy bekommerd is.
items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: Western Cape tuberculosis article: testing is free at public clinics, no appointment needed, 'just walk in'; the TB Control Programme page notes that for people living with HIV a cough of any duration is a warning sign. Nothing requires waiting two weeks.

items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: NSW Health 2024 lists blood-stained sputum; Western Cape tuberculosis article lists coughing up blood; Western Cape TB Control Programme: cough may be dry or productive.

items.blok: Die hoes wat aanhou
items.bron: Western Cape TB Control Programme page: the TB cough lasting longer than two weeks 'may be dry or productive'.

items.bewering: Koors: sy liggaam is warmer as gewoonlik. Iemand anders kan dit voel of met 'n termometer meet.
items.blok: Ander tekens en simptome van TB
items.bron: Western Cape tuberculosis article (fever or chills); NSW Health 2024 (fevers). Fever as a raised body temperature measurable by others: EBSCO Research Starters on signs.

items.bewering: Nagsweet: hy sweet snags deur sy klere.
items.blok: Ander tekens en simptome van TB
items.bron: Mayo Clinic 'Night sweats': repeated episodes of very heavy sweating during sleep, heavy enough to soak your nightclothes or bedding. Listed as a TB symptom by NSW Health 2024 and the Western Cape tuberculosis article.

items.blok: Ander tekens en simptome van TB
items.bron: Western Cape tuberculosis article: unintended weight loss; NSW Health 2024: unexplained weight loss.

items.bewering: Hy is heeldag moeg en sonder krag.
items.blok: Ander tekens en simptome van TB
items.bron: Western Cape tuberculosis article: constant tiredness; NSW Health 2024: always feeling tired.

items.blok: Ander tekens en simptome van TB
items.bron: Western Cape tuberculosis article and NSW Health 2024: loss of appetite.

items.blok: Die kliniek kan TB gesond maak
items.bron: Western Cape tuberculosis article: 'TB can be cured!' and TB testing and treatment are free at public clinics and hospitals. Stated as possibility ('kan'), not certainty; correct, since drug-resistant TB is harder to treat (same page).

items.blok: Die kliniek kan TB gesond maak
items.bron: Western Cape TB Control Programme: at the primary healthcare clinic the client gives 2 sputum samples that go to a lab; NSW Health 2024: a sputum test shows if TB germs are present.

items.blok: Die kliniek kan TB gesond maak
items.bron: Western Cape tuberculosis article 'TB can be cured!'; WHO SDG fact sheet 2017 'TB can be prevented, and it can be cured'; NSW Health 2024 'The disease can be cured with antibiotics'.

items.bewering: Die mens drink sy medisyne elke dag baie maande lank.
items.blok: Die kliniek kan TB gesond maak
items.bron: City of Johannesburg health department (joburg.org.za newsroom, March 2019, also reported by Citizen): patients take treatment every day for 180 days (six months); NSW Health 2024: at least six months; BMJ patient leaflet: at least six months. Drug-resistant TB longer. 'Baie maande' holds.

items.bewering: Hy hou aan ook nadat hy weer goed voel.
items.blok: Die kliniek kan TB gesond maak
items.bron: City of Johannesburg health department: every day for 180 days even if they feel better; Western Cape tuberculosis article 'Finish your treatment. Don't stop halfway'.

items.bewering: Dit gee hom die beste kans om gesond te word.
items.blok: Die kliniek kan TB gesond maak
items.bron: NSW Health 2024: 'People with TB can be cured if they complete treatment'; take all medicines exactly as prescribed without missing doses or stopping early. Stated as best chance, not a guarantee.

items.bewering: Die kliniek help hom om by te hou.
items.blok: Die kliniek kan TB gesond maak
items.bron: South African adherence support documented in the Cape Town Enhanced TB Adherence model delivered in primary health clinics (Karolinska Institutet open archive), lay health worker visits checking medication (Cape Town time-and-motion study), and a Limpopo DOTS study; NSW Health: a clinic nurse supervises treatment to support completion.

items.blok: Waar masels vandaan kom en hoe dit lyk
items.bron: CDC measles causes/transmission page: measles virus lives in the nose and throat mucus, spreads through coughing and sneezing, can live up to two hours in an airspace; CDC Measles Prevention and Treatment Overview: airborne precautions required.

items.bewering: Masels loop baie maklik oor.
items.blok: Waar masels vandaan kom en hoe dit lyk
items.bron: CDC measles transmission page: up to 90% of the people close to an infected person who are not immune will also become infected.

items.bewering: Die eerste tekens en simptome ...
items.blok: Waar masels vandaan kom en hoe dit lyk
items.bron: 'Eerste' here is a sequence (the early stage before the rash), not a priority claim. CDC signs-and-symptoms page: high fever, cough, runny nose and red watery eyes come first, rash 3 to 5 days later; NHS: measles usually begins with cold-like symptoms.

items.blok: Waar masels vandaan kom en hoe dit lyk
items.bron: NHS measles page: 'cold-like symptoms' including high temperature, runny or blocked nose, sneezing, cough. Mapping checked: the comparison breaks on the high fever, which an ordinary cold usually lacks, but the very next sentence names 'hoë koors', so a learner is not led to expect only a mild cold.

items.bewering: Die kind kry hoë koors, 'n loopneus en 'n hoes. Sy oë word ook rooi en seer.
items.blok: Waar masels vandaan kom en hoe dit lyk
items.bron: CDC signs and symptoms: high fever (may spike above 104 F), cough, runny nose, red watery eyes; NHS: red, sore, watery eyes.

items.blok: Waar masels vandaan kom en hoe dit lyk
items.bron: CDC: 'Measles rash appears 3 to 5 days after the first symptoms'; NHS: rash appears a few days after the cold-like symptoms.

items.bewering: Dit begin by die gesig en trek af oor die lyf.
items.blok: Waar masels vandaan kom en hoe dit lyk
items.bron: CDC: flat red spots appear on the face at the hairline, then spread downward to the neck, trunk, arms, legs and feet; NHS: starts on the face and behind the ears before spreading to the rest of the body.

items.bewering: 'n Kind met masels gaan ook kliniek toe.
items.blok: Wat die kliniek met masels doen
items.bron: CDC Measles Prevention and Treatment Overview: measles can need hospital care and complications should be managed under a healthcare provider. Note for the human only: CDC advises phoning the facility before arrival so infection control can be arranged; the lesson does not contradict this.

items.bewering: Maar geen medisyne maak hierdie virus dood nie.
items.blok: Wat die kliniek met masels doen
items.bron: CDC Measles Prevention and Treatment Overview (2026): 'There is no specific antiviral therapy that is approved ... for management of measles'; care is generally supportive. Ribavirin shows activity in the laboratory and is sometimes used in severe cases, but clinical efficacy data are lacking and it is not approved for measles (same CDC document); NEJM 1990 South African vitamin A trial background: 'no specific therapy for the disease'. True for anything a clinic gives.

items.bewering: Die kliniek help met die koors en sorg dat die kind genoeg drink.
items.blok: Wat die kliniek met masels doen
items.bron: NHS measles page: rest, plenty of fluids, paracetamol or ibuprofen for fever. Note for the human, not a finding: WHO and CDC also recommend two doses of vitamin A for children with measles where deficiency is common, and a South African trial (NEJM 1990) underlies that; the lesson does not present its list as complete, so the omission makes nothing false.

items.bewering: Die kliniek hou die kind fyn dop, want masels kan 'n mens baie siek maak.
items.blok: Wat die kliniek met masels doen
items.bron: CDC signs and symptoms: pneumonia is the most common cause of measles death in young children, encephalitis can occur, 1 to 3 of every 1,000 infected children die; CDC treatment overview: measles can cause serious illness requiring hospitalisation even in previously healthy people.

items.bewering: 'n Mens met TB is 'n gewone mens soos jy en ek. Die siekte is die probleem en nie die mens nie.
items.blok: 'n Mens met TB bly 'n gewone mens
items.bron: A value statement rather than a factual one; consistent with the Stop TB Partnership language guides 'Every Word Counts' (2015) and 'Words Matter' (2022), which aim to reduce TB stigma through people-centred language. Mapping checked: the comparison does not claim he cannot pass TB on; the next sentences deal with infectiousness and the clinic's decision, so it does not lead a learner to an unsafe conclusion.

items.bewering: Ná omtrent twee weke se medisyne gee hy die siekte gewoonlik nie meer oor nie.
items.blok: 'n Mens met TB bly 'n gewone mens
items.bron: NSW Health TB Fact Sheet (Mar 2024): 'In most cases, after two weeks of taking appropriate medication, people with TB disease will no longer spread TB germs.' Hong Kong Department of Health: great majority non-infectious after 2 weeks of effective treatment. Dharmadhikari et al. 2014, Int J Tuberc Lung Dis (South African study, PMC4692272): effective treatment rapidly renders drug-susceptible patients non-infectious; the two-week rule traces to Rouillon 1976. Western Cape article: spread is highest before treatment or in the early days of medication. Disclosed spread: a South African HealthInSite leaflet (hosted at hr.uct.ac.za) says 'in most cases ... two to four weeks'; a 2010 Lima study questioned the rule using culture conversion. The lesson hedges twice ('omtrent', 'gewoonlik') and does not tie return to school to the two weeks, which keeps it inside what the sources support. Drug-resistant TB is the main exception and 'gewoonlik' covers it.

items.bewering: Die kliniek sê wanneer hy weer skool of werk toe kan gaan.
items.blok: 'n Mens met TB bly 'n gewone mens
items.bron: HealthInSite 'TB and the workplace' (South African leaflet, hosted at hr.uct.ac.za): return to work should be based on medical clearance by a health-care professional; RIVM (Netherlands): the doctor and public health service say when it is safe to return to work, school or day care; Southern Nevada Health District: the TB clinic nurse tells you when you can return to work or school. Checked for implication: the lesson does not say he returns after two weeks; it hands that decision to the clinic, which is correct.

items.bewering: Gaan sit langs hom en vra hoe dit met hom gaan.
items.blok: 'n Mens met TB bly 'n gewone mens
items.bron: Checked for whether it follows: it comes directly after the clinic has decided he may return to school, i.e. after a health worker judged him non-infectious; NSW Health 2024: people with TB can return to normal activities while on treatment as long as they are no longer infectious. It is safe only because of that order; if the sentence were moved before the clinic sentence, or the clinic sentence cut, it would tell a child to sit beside someone who may still be infectious.

items.bewering: Die beste manier om masels te keer, is die inenting.
items.blok: Die inenting teen masels
items.bron: CDC Measles Prevention and Treatment Overview: 'MMR vaccination is the best way to prevent measles'; NHS: the vaccine is the best way to prevent measles.

items.bewering: Klein kinders kry hulle inentings by die kliniek.
items.blok: Die inenting teen masels
items.bron: Spotlight (1 Jul 2026) guide to South Africa's childhood vaccines: measles vaccine at 6 and 12 months; Bhekisisa/News24 2023: given free at public clinics under EPI-SA; GCIS 2004 health pocket guide lists immunisation among public clinic services. Also available privately, which the sentence does not exclude.

items.bewering: 'n Kind wat hierdie inenting gekry het, kry gewoonlik nie masels nie.
items.blok: Die inenting teen masels
items.bron: CDC Measles Vaccine Recommendations: one dose 93% effective, two doses 97% effective at preventing measles. 'Gewoonlik' is correct; it is not stated as certain.

items.blok: Die inenting teen masels
items.bron: CDC: up to 90% of close contacts who are NOT immune become infected, while vaccinated children are 93-97% protected; immunity status is therefore one reason exposed children differ. 'Een van die redes' does not overclaim.

items.bewering: tuberkulose: 'n Siekte wat deur kieme veroorsaak word, meestal in 'n mens se longe, dikwels met 'n hoes wat weke lank aanhou.
items.blok: begrip: tuberkulose
items.bron: Read alone. NSW Health 2024: caused by the bacteria Mycobacterium tuberculosis, most commonly affects the lungs but can affect other parts; persistent cough. 'Meestal' and 'dikwels' are correctly hedged.

items.bewering: masels: 'n Siekte wat deur 'n virus veroorsaak word en baie maklik oorloop, met hoë koors, rooi oë en 'n uitslag wat by die gesig begin.
items.blok: begrip: masels
items.bron: Read alone. CDC signs and symptoms (high fever, red watery eyes, rash beginning on the face at the hairline); CDC transmission (up to 90% of non-immune contacts infected).

items.bewering: kieme: Baie klein lewende dinge wat 'n mens siek kan maak.
items.blok: begrip: kieme
items.bron: Read alone. KidsHealth 'What Are Germs?': germs are tiny organisms, or living things, that can cause disease. Note for the human: whether viruses are living is disputed (ASU Ask a Biologist; Microbiology Society), and KidsHealth counts viruses among germs. This lesson never calls the measles virus a 'kiem' and uses 'kieme' only for TB bacteria, which are living, so nothing in the lesson becomes false.

items.bewering: virus: 'n Baie klein ding wat net binne-in 'n liggaam skade kan doen.
items.blok: begrip: virus
items.bron: Read alone. KidsHealth (parents): viruses are smaller than bacteria, not complete cells, and must live inside another cell to reproduce; Microbiology Society/ASU: outside a host cell viruses are inert, showing no metabolism or growth. Harm only once inside a body is accurate. It does not say the virus is harmless in the air (it survives there and infects when inhaled), and the lesson says measles goes through the air, so the two do not conflict.

items.bewering: simptoom: Iets wat wys dat 'n mens se gesondheid skeefloop en wat hy self ervaar, soos pyn, moegheid of naarheid.
items.blok: begrip: simptoom
items.bron: Read alone. Wikipedia 'Signs and symptoms'; EBSCO Research Starters (nausea, pain as symptoms); RxList 'symptom: any subjective evidence of disease'. All three examples are standard symptoms.

items.bewering: teken: Iets wat wys dat 'n mens se gesondheid skeefloop en wat 'n ander mens self kan sien, hoor, ruik of meet, ook al vertel hy niks, soos 'n uitslag of koors.
items.blok: begrip: teken
items.bron: Read alone. EBSCO Research Starters (fever, rash as signs); Wikipedia 'Signs and symptoms' (signs are objective, observable by others). Both examples hold.

items.bewering: inenting: 'n Inspuiting, of soms druppels in die mond, wat jou liggaam vooraf gereed maak om self teen 'n bepaalde siekte te veg.
items.blok: begrip: inenting
items.bron: Read alone. The South African EPI includes oral drops: oral polio at birth and 6 weeks (EPI-SA vaccinator manual on the health.gov.za knowledge hub; 2025 public schedule comparison) and oral rotavirus at 6 and 10 weeks; most others are injections. Preparing the body in advance to fight a specific disease is the standard description (CDC: vaccination prevents measles; KidsHealth). Combination vaccines target several particular diseases at once, which 'n bepaalde siekte' does not deny.

items.bewering: kliniek: 'n Plek in die gemeenskap waar mense gesondheidsorg kry, of hulle siek is of gesond.
items.blok: begrip: kliniek
items.bron: Read alone. GCIS 2004 health pocket guide: public clinic services include immunisation, maternity care, screening of children, health promotion and family planning (services for well people) as well as care for disease; Westonaria clinic opening (gov.za, 2012) and the Bluff PHC clinic (Durban) list the same mix.

opsomming: All 59 checked claims hold, including the TB two-week point (NSW Health gives it nearly word for word; one South African leaflet says two to four weeks, and the lesson's 'omtrent' and 'gewoonlik' cover that) and the clinic deciding when he returns to school; three things a person should know: the qualifiers 'Nie almal wat die kieme inasem, word siek nie' and 'kry gewoonlik nie masels nie' are what keep block 1's 'kry so die siekte' from reading as certain, and 'Gaan sit langs hom' is safe only because it follows the clinic's decision, so none of these may be cut or reordered; separately, zoonotic TB does reach people through unpasteurised milk in rural South Africa, which the 'not from shared food' sentence does not touch but a person may want to know.
